title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and say your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use threats or urgent language to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to verify your Social Security number or your benefits will be stopped immediately."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Social Security or Medicare number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text message saying you have a package waiting and need to click a link to reschedule delivery or pay a small fee. The link leads to a fake website that tries to steal your information.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address and pay $1.99 by clicking this link: [fake link]"
red_flags: Requests for payment or personal info
what_to_do: Do not click any links or give out information; delete the message.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails that look like they are from the Social Security Administration. They claim there is a problem with your account and ask you to click a link or download an attachment.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please click here to verify your information."
red_flags: Requests to click links or download files
what_to_do: Do not click on links or download anything; report the email to the real Social Security Administration.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook or another social media site quickly becomes friendly and romantic. After building trust, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I love you and want to visit, but I need help paying for my plane ticket. Can you send me money?"
red_flags: Requests for money or gift cards
Refusal to meet in person or video chat
what_to_do: Never send money or gift cards to someone you have not met in person.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus and must call a number for help. The person on the phone asks for remote access to your computer or payment for fake repairs.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-800-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pressure to let someone control your computer
Requests for payment in gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number; use your own trusted tech support if you need help.
